title: Programming languages
text: IEC 61131-3 defines Ladder Diagram (LD), Function Block Diagram (FBD), Structured Text (ST), Sequential Function Chart (SFC) and (deprecated in edition 3) Instruction List. Rockwell RLL is a vendor implementation of Ladder Diagram; Rockwell ST follows IEC Structured Text syntax.

title: Identifiers
text: Identifiers start with a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits or single underscores. They are case-insensitive and must not collide with keywords such as IF, THEN, END_IF, CASE, FOR, TRUE, FALSE. Avoid consecutive or trailing underscores for portability; Rockwell limits tag names to 40 characters.

title: Elementary data types
text: BOOL is a single bit, INT is 16-bit signed, DINT is 32-bit signed, REAL is 32-bit IEEE floating point and STRING holds characters. Use BOOL for discrete IO and commands, DINT for counters and millisecond presets, REAL for analog values and setpoints in engineering units.

title: Structured Text statements
text: ST assignments use ':=' and end with ';'. Conditional logic uses IF ... THEN ... ELSIF ... ELSE ... END_IF; and CASE selector OF ... END_CASE;. Comments are written (* like this *). Boolean expressions use AND, OR, XOR and NOT.

title: Ladder rung evaluation
text: A rung is evaluated left to right: series contacts form an AND, parallel branches form an OR. In Rockwell RLL text, XIC examines a bit for ON, XIO examines for OFF, OTE energizes an output while the rung is true, BST/NXB/BND delimit a parallel branch.

title: Start/stop seal-in (latching) circuit
text: A motor start/stop circuit places the start push button in parallel with the run output (seal-in contact), followed in series by the normally-closed stop push button and all permissives, then OTE(run). Example: BST XIC(Start_PB) NXB XIC(Motor_Run) BND XIC(Stop_PB) XIC(EStop_OK) OTE(Motor_Run).

title: Emergency stop interlock
text: Emergency stop must override all other functions and de-energize hazardous motion. Every motor run, start or contactor output must be conditioned in series by the healthy status of the E-stop safety circuit (e.g. XIC(EStop_OK)). E-stop contacts must never be placed inside a parallel branch where another path could bypass them.

title: Latched outputs
text: Avoid OTL/OTU latch instructions for motor outputs: after a power cycle or E-stop the output may remain latched and restart unexpectedly. Prefer seal-in circuits with OTE so loss of the permissive drops the output. If latches are required, unlatch on E-stop and on first scan.

title: Restart after stop
text: Resetting an emergency stop must not by itself restart the machine; a deliberate start command is required. Use edge-triggered or momentary start push buttons and require the run seal-in to be re-established after any stop or fault.

title: Normally-closed stop inputs
text: Stop push buttons and safety inputs are wired normally-closed so a broken wire is detected as a stop. In logic, examine them with XIC (true when healthy), not XIO.

title: On-delay timers
text: TON delays an output: Q (Rockwell .DN) becomes TRUE after IN has been TRUE for PT (Rockwell .PRE in ms). Use a start-warning horn timed with TON before starting conveyors, and qualify the motor run output with the timer done bit.

title: Unique physical addresses
text: Each physical IO point must be mapped to exactly one tag. Two tags aliasing the same input or output address cause conflicting writes or misleading diagnostics. Keep internal (memory) tags unaddressed.

title: Tag naming conventions
text: Prefix tags with the equipment identifier (e.g. P101 for a pump, M200 for a motor) followed by the signal function: P101_Start_PB, P101_Stop_PB, P101_Run (command output), P101_Running (feedback), P101_Fault, P101_Speed_SP (setpoint, REAL).

title: HMI layout
text: HMI screens should group controls by equipment, place start/stop buttons together with the running indicator, show analog values as numeric displays with engineering units, and use colour sparingly: grey for normal, colour reserved for abnormal and alarm states.

title: HMI tag binding
text: Buttons and indicators bind to BOOL tags, numeric displays bind to INT, DINT or REAL tags. Every HMI object must reference an existing controller or program tag; unresolved references show as errors at runtime.

title: Alarm management
text: Alarms indicate abnormal conditions that require an operator response. Assign severity by consequence and urgency: CRITICAL for safety (e.g. E-stop), HIGH for process stops such as jams or motor faults, MEDIUM/LOW for advisories.

title: Program organisation
text: Organise logic in one subroutine per equipment module (e.g. P101_Control) called from the program MainRoutine with JSR. Keep each routine focused, comment every rung, and avoid writing the same output from more than one rung (double coil).

title: Scan cycle
text: PLC programs execute cyclically: read inputs, execute logic top to bottom, write outputs. An output written in two places takes the last value written in the scan, which hides logic errors; use a single OTE per output.
